about: The computed national-team seasons between the computed World Cups, 1962/63 to 1992/93 (docs/design/football-years.md, "Computed national-team seasons"): every source pinned and every constant of the method, so a later change of the built-in data changes nothing. npm run sync:national-team-seasons reads the sources from data-src/ into the committed facts (scripts/data/national-team-seasons/), and npm run build:national-team-seasons turns the facts into public/football/nt-<year>.json. elo, strength, xi and profile are the World Cup seasons' (scripts/data/world-cup-seasons.json), equal by test.
decided: 2026-11-13: the user asked to cover the year gaps in every sport ("there are many year gaps in the various sports can you cover them"). The seasons between the World Cups are computed like them: the user approved computed football ratings for the 1960s to 1980s on 2026-11-09 (national-team Elo adjusted per player, labelled as computed), and the World Cup seasons shipped on 2026-11-10. Claude chose the rest: each nation's players from Wikidata's national-team records (their stints and caps), which the World Cup seasons left out; its strength from its Elo on 1 July of the season's end year, by the World Cup seasons' line; the XI by caps a year and its order by Ballon d'Or votes and caps.

wikidata.name: Wikidata: the men's national association football teams (instances of Q135408445) and their players' memberships (P54) with start (P580), end (P582), matches played (P1350) and goals (P1351); the players' names, dates of birth (P569), English Wikipedia articles and positions (P413)
wikidata.endpointNote: QLever (University of Freiburg) answers SPARQL over the whole Wikidata dump; qlever.dev has no robots.txt. The Wikidata Query Service and Wikidata's API are disallowed for every agent by their robots.txt (scripts/lib/wikidata-sparql.mjs).

ballonDor.name: English Wikipedia, "<year> Ballon d'Or": the voting tables (the votes are France Football's)
ballonDor.fetched: The article pages (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/<title>), one every 2 s: robots.txt disallows /w/ and /api/ to every user agent and allows /wiki/. Sixteen were saved for the World Cup seasons on 2026-11-09, the other sixteen on 2026-11-13. A page saved again shows the same revision, not always the same bytes.

elo.formula: R' = R + K × G × (W − We), We = 1 / (1 + 10^(−dr / 400)), dr = R_home − R_away + home (none at a neutral venue); W is 1, ½ or 0, a match level after extra time a draw

start.rule: A team starts at 1500, or at 1300 when its first match in the results is in a year after 1930.

elo.goals: G is 1 for a margin of 0 or 1, 1.5 for 2, 1.75 for 3 and 1.75 + (N − 3) / 8 for N of 4 or more
elo.date: The ratings the day after the final: every match up to and including the final's day

strength.rule: T = best − perHundredElo × (E_best − E) / 100: E is the nation's Elo, E_best the best Elo among the teams that played in the four years before.
strength.calibration: best is the strongest built-in nation's strength (EA FC 27 + FM 26, 2026/27). 3.2 points per 100 Elo gives the game's football model (rate 1.28·e^(1.5·tanh(0.075Δ / 1.5)), Poisson goals) Elo's expected score within 0.0015 for gaps of 50 to 300 Elo, and the 173 built-in strengths regress on their 2026 Elo from the same results with a slope of 3.20 (r 0.895).

profileSource: The mean sorted deviation from the XI's mean of the 32 strongest built-in XIs (2026/27), to one decimal.

selection.rule: A nation's pool for the season ending in Y: the players of its team with a Wikidata stint covering Y − 1 or Y (a stint Wikidata has not closed, such as Paolo Maldini's for Italy from 1988, ends as its caps would run out at 8 a year: start + ⌈caps / 8⌉ − 1; one with neither end nor caps is left out), each with his stint's caps a year, caps / (end − start + 1), halved when the stint covers only one of the two years. A player in two nations' pools plays for the one where that figure is higher. The XI: for each role (1 GK, 4 DF, 4 MF, 2 FW) the pool's players of that position, the highest figure first (then the most caps for the team by then, then the lower Wikidata id); a role short of them takes the highest figures left. A nation fields a team when its pool holds at least 11 players with a position, one a goalkeeper, it played a full international in the four years before, and its shape takes part that year. The XI's order: Ballon d'Or points of the season's two years, then the caps for the team by the season's end (each stint's caps spread evenly over its years), then the figure, then the lower Wikidata id.

positionsNote: Every position item the answers hold for these players, read 2026-11-13: association football's (P641 Q2736) and the general goalkeeper, defender, attacker and winger. Left out as other sports' or no position: Q179789 (handball goalkeeper), Q2304909 (ice hockey defenseman), Q543457 (ice hockey forward), Q2827965 (ice hockey winger), Q2717266 (rugby union fullback), Q5508224 (rugby league fullback), Q1985622 (military defense), Q526301 (utility player), and coaching roles.

names.ignoreTeamsNote: Q1516237 the pre-1950 IFA Ireland team (not the Republic of Ireland), Q922698 Italy's under-21s, Q775352 the "Golden Team" (Hungary's 1950s side, not a team of its own), Q918214 Great Britain's Olympic team, Q1413794 the FLN team (1958–1962, no FIFA member), Q738846 the Basque Country's regional side (no FIFA member): classed as men's national teams on Wikidata, but none is a FIFA member's full national team.

Soviet Union.why: no team after 1991/92: its players played for the CIS, then for their republics

Russia.why: no team before 16 August 1992, when Russia first played; the Soviet Union and the CIS played for it

Czechia.why: no team before 23 February 1994, when the Czech Republic first played; Czechoslovakia played for it

CIS.why: its last match was on 18 June 1992, before the season; Russia and the other republics played for themselves

nations.byYearNote: Where Wikidata keeps one team across two federations, or a team began after the season: SFR and FR Yugoslavia are one team (to 2003), and FR Yugoslavia, Serbia's shape (688), was suspended from 31 May 1992 to December 1994 (src/data/footballFederations.js), so its players field no team in 1991/92 and 1992/93; the Soviet Union's players of autumn 1991 and the CIS's of 1992 are one side in 1991/92, the CIS (643); Russia's own team, whose stints start in 1992 (a year, not a day), first played after that season, and the Czech Republic's from 1994: a stint of theirs dated earlier is the predecessor's and is left out.

names.noTeamNote: Countries with no shape on the map: the small associations the world map leaves out as the built-in season does (Malta, San Marino, the Faroe Islands, Liechtenstein, Singapore). Their players field no team. East Germany has a shape of its own on the map of its years, to 1990 (src/data/teams.js HISTORIC_NATIONS), and fields its team in the seasons up to 1988/89; after them its land is Germany's.
names.ballonDorPlayersNote: Votes whose link is a redirect to another title of the same man's article (Jef Jurion to Armand Jurion, Fedor to Fyodor Cherenkov, Harald to Toni Schumacher), each the Wikidata item whose English article the redirect leads to, checked by hand on 2026-11-13.
